newsitem.title: FINLAND: Midsummer might in Nokia pumps Helsinki higher.
newsitem.headline: Midsummer might in Nokia pumps Helsinki higher.

text.p: Shares in Finland showed no sign of a post-midsummer hangover on Monday -- Nokia punched sharply ahead and indices defied wobbles elsewhere in Europe.
"The uptrend has been so steep today, we could be a little lower tomorrow." one broker said, referring to a slight row-back in late Helsinki trade as U.S. markets made an unsteady start.

Derivatives trading on the SOM options bourse only got going late due to technical problems, but the FOX index managed a 0.81 pct gain to 1,079.10. The all-share HEX broke more all-time high ground, adding 1.01 percent to 3,157.88.
Volume was a hefty 800 million markka, over half in Nokia.
Nokia opened with ground to make up after strong gains in the U.S. on Friday, and at one stage outpaced its Wall St rise, closing up 12.00 markka at 377.00.

Brokers offered a range of explanations from short-covering after recent dips and talk of a new U.S. "buy" recommendation, to a positive response to Nokia joining a U.S.-Japanese group setting standards for personal digital assistants.
One broker saw room for Nokia to head to FIM 400 this week.
Also gaining with a fair chunk of the action was Merita, up 0.40 markka at 17.40. Brokers cited firm U.S. treasuries -- but banks in London were also lively amid bid talk in Natwest.

Amer gained 1.00 markka to 95.00 after its vote-heavy K-shareholders called off a deal to sell control to British investor Lord Moyne, which had initially sparked gains in the stock but was subsequently viewed with suspicion.
"There was mistrust about Lord Moyne," one broker said. But trade in Amer remained quite hesitant amid revived uncertainty about the eventual control of the sporting goods company.
